newsitem.title: USA: NYC plans $875 mln refunding before June 30.
newsitem.headline: NYC plans $875 mln refunding before June 30.

text.p: New York City, which said its huge sale of tax-exempt and taxable bonds was "well-received" by investors, said it plans to tap the debt markets again before June 30 with an $875 million refunding.
The refunding hinges on market conditions, the city said in a prepared release, adding it also expected to sell competitively $200 million to $300 million of tax-exempt bonds during the same period.
The city's 1997 fiscal year ends June 30.
New York City earlier sold $900 million of tax-exempt bonds through a syndicate led by Smith Barney, plus $122 million of taxable bonds, which were won by Morgan Stanley.

Another $50 million of taxable, floating-rate bonds were sold in Europe. The city noted the floaters were priced at the same 28-basis point spread over the London Interbank Offered Rate as similar notes sold by New York City in January, although rates have risen several basis points since then.

"The fact that the trading value of New York City paper has improved over the past year and one-half compared to the overall municipal market indicates that investors have an increasing recognition of the city's improving economic and financial prospects," said Mayor Rudolph Giuliani, in prepared remarks.

About $722 million of the bonds, including the $120 million of taxable debt, will pay for part of the city's capital program. The other $350 million, including the $50 million of floating-rate bonds, were a refunding that saved $16 million on a present value basis and gave the city $18 million for its fiscal 1998 budget.

The city comptroller, Alan Hevesi, pointed to the $304 million of retail orders placed during the presale period and the widespread interest seen in Europe as evidence of the success of the debt sales. "It is good news that this was the fourth largest retail order period in the city's experience and that the Euronotes were placed with an increasingly diverse group of European investors."
